description.narrative:
The Employment Advocacy for Rural Youth project is aimed at increasing recognition for non-formally educated youths with demonstrated skills and potential for career development into formal employment in Abuja, Nigeria.
Despite the Nigeria Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) which enables recognition of non-formal learning, non-formally educated and rural youths face persistent employmentbarriers as employers continue to prioritize formal certifications over demonstrated skills. Poor policy awareness and implementation means these competencies remain undervalued in hiring processes. This disconnect between policy intent and market practice perpetuates economic exclusion of capable but non-formally educated youth.
With a fast-rising population of 230 million, a working-age population of 116.6 million and youths comprising 75% of that population, data from the Nigeria’s Bureau of Statistics shows that non-formally educated youth which comprise 27% of the working-age population “are still stuck ininformal or underemployment”. While these youths possess valuable skills and competencies, rigid certification requirements create systemic barriers to their economic participation. This project advocates for alternative competency evaluation standards with employers, focusing on demonstrated abilities rather than formal credentials. This approach provides an immediate, scalable solution that leverages existing corporate inclusion policies while creating sustainable pathways for marginalized youth to access employment opportunities.
We will advocate for the private sector to incorporate the NSQF into their hiring policies and facilitate dialogue at the grassroot level by engaging governmentand private stakeholders. Using traditional and non-traditional media, we will promote awareness of the Framework, and demonstrate the value of diverse learning achievements to employers which will lead to increased acceptance of alternative qualifications, ultimately leading to meaningful job access for capable youth often overlooked due to lack of formal certifications.

participating-org.narrative:
Teach the Child is a female-led, youth-led organisation which began as a solution to the public education crisis in Nigeria during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Our Vision is to raise economically self-sufficient adults. Our mission is for every child, in spite of their background, to become economically self-sufficient adults through improved literacy and digital skills. To achieve this, weutilize innovative educational technologies, board and tabletop games which have been proven to help improve dexterity, recognitionand retention in children, and Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) approaches. Through these efforts, we strive to bridge the gap between the privileged and the disadvantaged, ultimately empowering children to reach their full potential.
In 2023, Teach the Child was awarded the Development Grant Award by the Nigerian Youth Futures Fund (NYFF), supported by LEAP Africa, MacArthur Foundation and Luminate. This award fostered youth involvement in education advocacy, awareness raising about curriculum reform, and strengthenedstakeholder commitment to improving basic education in Nigeria. Teach the Child also serves as a platform for youths to build theirprofessional capacity in education policy influencing, community engagement, 21st-century teaching/learning skills and education inthe public system through internships. Our interns come from several countries across Africa.
The depth of the work carried out bythe Initiative has led to recognition by the U.S. Department of State andsupport from several institutions such as the University of Virginia (UVA) in America, African Leadership Academy in South Africa, and Civil Society in Development/Crossing Borders in Denmark.
